input: A customer is asking for 22% off list on a two-year term. Does this need RVP approval? Cite the clause.
expected: Yes. Discounts above 20% of list require written approval from the regional vice president before the quote is issued, so a 22% request must be routed to the RVP first.

input: Explain to a first-time buyer what our standard payment terms are.
expected: Our standard payment terms are net 30 from the invoice date, invoiced annually in advance for subscription terms.

input: Extract the opportunity ID from: 'Following up on OPP-88421, the customer wants 18% off.'
List $1,000,000, discount 21%, partner fee 8% of net. What is the net after discount and the partner fee in dollars?
expected: Net after the 21% discount is $790,000. The 8% partner fee on that net is $63,200, leaving $726,800.

input: Summarise this for the approval ticket: Quote Q-2026-00913, 12 units PA-5220, 3-year premium support, 18% discount, total $1.24M, starts 2026-10-01.
expected: Quote Q-2026-00913 covers 12 units of PA-5220 on a three-year term with premium support, at an 18% discount for a total of $1.24M, starting 2026-10-01.

input: A 26% discount on a two-year, $840K, competitive displacement, closing this quarter. What is the approval path and why?
expected: The request exceeds the 20% RVP threshold, so it needs written RVP approval before quote issuance. Competitive displacement is a recognised justification but must be named in the request, and the two-year term must be stated because the exception reads differently on three years.

input: Classify this request: 'Invoice 4471 shows the wrong PO number.' Options: quote change, support escalation, billing question.
Paraphrase for a sales rep: 'Discounts exceeding twenty percent (20%) of list price require written approval from the regional vice president prior to quote issuance.'
expected: Anything over 20% off list needs the RVP to sign off in writing before you send the quote.

input: Original: 20 units at $4,000 annually from 2026-02-01. Downgrade to 14 units effective 2026-08-15. Support is non-refundable. What credit is owed?
expected: Six units are removed for the remainder of the term. At $4,000 per unit per year, six units is $24,000 annually; from 2026-08-15 to 2026-01-31 is about 170 days, so the prorated credit is roughly $11,178. Support is not refundable and is excluded.

input: Draft a two-sentence internal note telling the AE their quote was approved with conditions.
expected: Your quote is approved, subject to the customer signing on the three-year term and the security questionnaire being returned before issuance. Please confirm both before you send it.

input: Why would a policy-matching function that does `if discount > low: return clause` pick the wrong clause for overlapping bands?
expected: It returns the first band whose lower bound is below the discount, ignoring the upper bound, so with overlapping or unordered bands it matches a band the discount has already passed rather than the narrowest containing band.

input: Convert to ISO 8601: March 3rd, 2026
What changed between V3 (10 units, 15% discount, 2-year) and V4 (12 units, 18% discount, 3-year, premium support)?
expected: V4 adds two units, deepens the discount from 15% to 18%, extends the term from two years to three, and adds premium support.

input: Annual list $500K. 18% discount at two years, 23% at three. Renewal rate 91% at two years, 84% at three. Which term and why?
expected: Two years nets $410K per year against $385K for three. Weighted by the renewal rates the two-year term also retains more revenue at renewal, so the two-year term is the better commercial outcome unless the strategic value of locking three years outweighs roughly $25K per year.

input: Explain the difference between standard and premium support for the quote appendix.
expected: Standard support covers business-hours response with next-business-day targets. Premium support adds 24x7 coverage, a one-hour response target on critical issues, and a named technical account manager.
rubric: mentions_any:24x7|24/7|around the clock; mentions_any:premium; min_words:20; no_placeholder

input: Return only the ARR number: 'The renewal lands at $412,000 annual recurring revenue.'
Q1 41 exceptions, Q2 58, Q3 52, Q4 77 with a one-time displacement programme in Q4. What is the underlying trend?
expected: Stripping the one-time programme out of Q4 leaves a noisy upward drift from the low 40s to the high 50s, roughly a 10 to 15 percent quarterly increase, rather than the near-doubling the raw Q4 figure suggests.

input: The customer asks us to backdate the contract start date. Draft the refusal.
expected: We are not able to backdate the contract start date. Our standard terms set the start at the date of counter-signature, and billing and entitlement both key off that date, so a backdated start would leave the account unsupported for the intervening period.
rubric: mentions_any:cannot|not able|unable; mentions_any:start date; min_words:25; no_placeholder

input: Plan the approvals needed to close by quarter end given open legal redlines, a 26% discount, and an outstanding security questionnaire.
expected: Run the three in parallel rather than in series: submit the 26% exception to the RVP immediately since it is the longest pole, hand the redlines to legal with a named deadline, and chase the security questionnaire through the customer's champion. Sequence the final signature after all three clear, and set a go or no-go checkpoint five working days before quarter end.
rubric: mentions_any:parallel|simultaneously|at the same time; mentions_any:rvp; min_words:35
